**FCCPS AI Advisory Committee Minutes**

**Date of Meeting**

Friday, April 24, 2026

**Location of Meeting**

FCCPS School Board Office (Multi-Purpose Room)

**Time of Meeting**

8:30–\~11:43 AM (in-person; extended working session). Otter AI recording header: 8:41 AM–\~11:43 AM.

| **Members Present:
Members Absent:** | Members Present:
Co-Chairs: John Black (Chair); Adriana Palacios Bonarrigo (Vice Chair)
School Board Liaisons (non-voting): Jerrod Anderson; Bethany Henderson
Division Staff Liaisons: None noted
Committee Members (present): Elizabeth Chua; Anubav Vasudevan; Jillian Burkley; Tom Sabo; David Berol; Susan Nelson; Thomas Colvin
Visitors/Public: Sarah Debus-Sherrill
Members Absent:
Tina Beaty | |-----------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

from Meeting 6 were approved by unanimous voice vote. Motion was made by Tom Sabo and seconded by Adriana Palacios Bonarrigo.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Public Comments**                                               | Sarah Debus-Sherrill attended as a member of the public and, when invited during deliberations, introduced herself and shared concerns regarding student-facing AI in elementary grades, developmental appropriateness, and social-emotional harms. Tina Beaty was absent but had submitted written comments that were considered during discussion of the student-use sections.

|
| **Extended Working Session Purpose / Draft Status**               | Chair restated that Meeting 7 was an extended triage-and-revision session intended to move the consolidated draft package into Board-ready form, not to reopen every policy dispute. The committee reviewed the integrated package as it stood after Meeting 6: consolidated WS-POL sections in committee voice, supporting workstream material, and annotated references in lieu of line-by-line inline citations.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **Triage of Remaining Policy Issues**                             | The committee identified WS-POL-E (staff and teacher use of AI) and WS-POL-F+G (student use

by grade band) as the highest-priority unresolved sections. Related issues in disclosure, consent, detector language, overall policy posture, section placement, and Board-facing clarity were treated as cross-cutting issues to resolve only to the extent necessary for accuracy, neutrality, and usability.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **WS-POL-E — Staff and Teacher Use of AI**                        | Members revisited unresolved differences regarding AI use in teacher feedback and evaluation, including the distinction between formative and evaluative feedback, the degree of required transparency/traceability, and whether detector-related arguments were adequately represented. The section was not fully closed in-room. Thomas Colvin was asked to redraft Section E in coordination with Susan Nelson and David Berol, with comments due by Sunday night.

|
| **WS-POL-F+G — Student Use, Grade Bands, and AI Literacy**        | The committee devoted substantial time to the student-use sections, especially the relationship between AI literacy, developmental appropriateness, and direct student interaction with AI tools. Discussion emphasized the need to distinguish learning about AI from direct student-facing use of AI, particularly in younger grades, and to preserve the range of views on how restrictive elementary guidance should be. By voice vote, the committee approved integration of two edits proposed by Elizabeth Chua in these sections, including grade-band language and resilience-related phrasing. Elizabeth Chua agreed to prepare revised text for Sections F and G; Jillian Burkley agreed to review that revision. |
| **Integrity, Disclosure, and Detector Language**                  | The committee revisited detector posture, disclosure expectations, and process-evidence language as part of the integrity and student-use framework. Chair took a show of han

ds on a provisional non-use posture for AI detectors in integrity decisions until stronger evidence of reliability and clearer due-process protections exist; all nine committee members present supported that posture. Members also discussed the need for clearer definitions around “AI assistance,” disclosure expectations, and high-stakes work.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Section C / Scope and Triaging Language**                       | The committee agreed that the triaging/scope language in Section C would be more useful if condensed and re-homed into Section A and related sections rather than preserved as a stand-alone section. Thomas Colvin volunteered to pull the scope and triage material upward and simplify it. Motion to proceed in that direction carried by voice vote.

|
| **Public Accountability, Consent, and Section L**                 | The committee reviewed notice/consent language, including whether the wording was operationally realistic and whether it improperly suggested closure on implementation questions that remained unresolved. Discussion also included whether language about “minority stakeholders” was the right formulation. Section L was narrowed further and left for cleanup in the post-meeting revision round.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Board-Facing Clarity, Declarative Language, and Bibliography**  | Bethany Henderson urged the committee to lead each section with clear recommendations, use more declarative language, and include a visible bibliography or references appendix to demonstrate the depth of research and deliberation behind the package. The

committee agreed that the final Board-facing packet should prioritize usability and credibility: a concise synopsis first, supported by a calibrated references section and longer appendices.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Governance, Reassessment, and Budget / Workforce Implications** | The committee discussed adding language on ongoing review of AI policy and related guidance, including the possibility of a standing-review or standing-committee mechanism, as well as associated staffing, workload, and budget implications. By voice vote, the committee approved adding standing-review language to Section O and related implementation/budget language to Section N.

|
| **Assignments, Deadlines, and Adjournment**                       | Section owners were given until Sunday night to revise text, with the Chair to circulate a clean integrated copy with accepted changes early Monday morning. Chair also requested short committee-member bios for use in the April 28 School Board work session materials. Motion to adjourn carried, and the meeting adjourned at approximately 11:43 AM.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

-   **John Black:** Review Tina Beaty’s written comments on student use and AI literacy, decide what will be incorporated, and send her a readout of the committee’s decisions.
-   **John Black:** Draft a concise, declarative executive summary for the policy package, compile a calibrated bibliography/references appendix, perform a final clarity-and-consistency pass, and circulate a clean copy of the revised package with accepted track changes by early Monday morning.
-   **John Black:** Prepare short committee-member bios for possible use in the April 28 School Board work session materials.
-   **Thomas Colvin:** Revise Section E in coordination with Susan Nelson and David Berol, preserving the actual disagreement on teacher feedback, evaluation, transparency, and detector posture.
-   **Elizabeth Chua:** Revise Sections F and G based on the meeting discussion, including grade-band language, AI-literacy framing, developmental safeguards, monitoring, and equity considerations.
-   **Jillian Burkley:** Review Elizabeth Chua’s revised F/G draft and provide any additional comments or edits before Sunday night.
-   **Thomas Colvin:** Re-home and condense the scope/triaging language from

Section C into Section A and related sections.
-   **Relevant section owners / contributors:** Review whether additional language is needed on social-emotional and mental-health risks, harmful content exposure, and related student-safety concerns, and revise consent language for clarity and operational realism.
